title: Azure Fundamentals
subtitle: Jeopardy Review

jeopardyFormatExample.clueText: Microsoft 365 and Dynamics 365 fall into this cloud service model where Microsoft manages everything from the hardware up through the application

categoryLegend: Cloud Concepts & Models: IaaS, PaaS, SaaS, public, private, hybrid.  Azure Global Infrastructure: regions, Availability Zones, region pairs.  Azure Compute & Networking: VMs, App Service, Functions, VNet, NSG, ExpressRoute.  Azure Storage & Databases: Blob tiers, LRS, ZRS, GRS, SQL Database, Cosmos DB.  Identity & Resource Hierarchy: Microsoft Entra ID, RBAC, management group, subscription, resource group.  Management & Governance: Azure Policy, locks, Blueprints, ARM, Cost Management, Advisor.

clues.clue: In this cloud service model, the customer manages the operating system and above, while Microsoft manages the physical hardware and network — Azure Virtual Machines is the primary example.
clues.response: What is IaaS (Infrastructure as a Service)?
clues.explain: IaaS gives customers the most control: they provision VMs and are responsible for the OS, patches, and everything above. Microsoft handles the physical datacenter, networking hardware, and hypervisor.

clues.clue: Microsoft 365 and Dynamics 365 fall into this cloud service model, where Microsoft manages everything from the hardware up through the application layer.
clues.response: What is SaaS (Software as a Service)?
clues.explain: In SaaS, the provider manages the full stack including the application itself. Customers only manage their data and user access — everything else is Microsoft's responsibility.

clues.clue: Under the Azure shared responsibility model, this class of data — along with user identities — remains the customer's responsibility regardless of which cloud service model is used.
clues.response: What is customer data (or: data and identity)?
clues.explain: No matter whether a workload runs on IaaS, PaaS, or SaaS, the customer always owns responsibility for their data and for managing user identities and access. Physical security of datacenters is always Microsoft's.

clues.clue: Azure App Service and Azure Functions both fall into this service model, where Microsoft manages the underlying operating system and runtime so developers focus solely on application code.
clues.response: What is PaaS (Platform as a Service)?
clues.explain: PaaS removes OS and runtime management from the customer. Azure App Service hosts web apps and APIs; Azure Functions extends PaaS to serverless event-driven code — in both cases Microsoft patches and manages the platform.

clues.clue: This Azure deployment model uses Azure Stack HCI to run Azure-consistent services in a customer-owned datacenter, bridging on-premises infrastructure with the public cloud.
clues.response: What is the hybrid cloud deployment model?
clues.explain: A hybrid cloud connects private on-premises infrastructure with the Azure public cloud. Azure Stack HCI is Microsoft's hyperconverged solution that brings Azure services — including Arc management — to customer-operated hardware.

clues.clue: This is the term for a set of datacenters deployed within a latency-defined perimeter and connected through a dedicated regional low-latency network — Azure has more than 60 of them worldwide.
clues.explain: An Azure region is a geographic area containing one or more physically close datacenters linked by a high-speed network. Customers choose a region to deploy resources, trading off latency, compliance, and available service SKUs.

clues.clue: Within a single Azure region, these are the physically separate datacenters — each with independent power, cooling, and networking — that protect against a single-datacenter failure.
clues.explain: Availability Zones are distinct physical locations within one Azure region. By deploying across at least two zones, customers achieve high availability against the failure of any single datacenter, while remaining within the same region.

clues.clue: This Microsoft-defined pairing links two Azure regions within the same geography — such as East US and West US — to enable cross-region disaster recovery and staggered platform maintenance.
clues.response: What is an Azure region pair?
clues.explain: Microsoft pairs each region with another in the same geography. During planned maintenance, only one region in a pair is updated at a time. GRS replication automatically uses the paired region as the secondary target.

clues.clue: These physically and logically isolated Azure environments — one operated for the US government and one operated by 21Vianet in China — are examples of this Azure infrastructure category.
clues.explain: Sovereign regions are isolated Azure instances that meet specific compliance or regulatory requirements. The Azure Government cloud serves US federal, state, and local agencies; Azure China is operated by 21Vianet to comply with Chinese regulations.

clues.clue: Although an Availability Zone protects against a single-datacenter failure, a customer who needs protection against the failure of an ENTIRE Azure region must use this infrastructure-level feature instead.
clues.response: What is an Azure region pair (or: cross-region replication / GRS)?
clues.explain: Availability Zones only span datacenters within one region, so a region-wide outage still affects all zones together. Cross-region protection requires region pairs, which place a secondary copy of data in a geographically distant paired region.

clues.clue: This Azure networking resource creates an isolated, private network within Azure where customers define their own IP address space, subnets, and routing rules.
clues.explain: A VNet is the fundamental networking building block in Azure. It provides isolation and segmentation, allowing resources to communicate securely within Azure and to control connectivity to the internet or on-premises environments.

clues.clue: This Azure compute service is serverless and event-triggered — you pay only per execution, and Microsoft manages all underlying infrastructure including the OS and runtime.
clues.explain: Azure Functions is a Function-as-a-Service (FaaS) offering. Code runs in response to triggers such as HTTP requests, timer schedules, or queue messages, and billing is based on execution count and duration rather than reserved capacity.

clues.clue: Unlike a VPN Gateway — which routes traffic over the encrypted public internet — this Azure connectivity service provides a DEDICATED PRIVATE connection from an on-premises network to Azure that does not traverse the public internet.
clues.explain: ExpressRoute establishes a private, high-bandwidth connection between on-premises infrastructure and Microsoft's network through a connectivity provider. Because traffic never touches the public internet, ExpressRoute offers lower latency, higher reliability, and predictable throughput compared to VPN Gateway.

clues.clue: This Azure service is a stateful network filtering resource attached to a subnet or NIC that allows or denies inbound and outbound traffic based on source/destination IP, port, and protocol rules.
clues.response: What is a Network Security Group (NSG)?
clues.explain: An NSG contains a list of security rules evaluated in priority order. Because NSGs are stateful, a rule permitting inbound traffic automatically allows the corresponding outbound return traffic without requiring a separate outbound rule.

clues.clue: While Azure Load Balancer operates at Layer 4 and distributes TCP/UDP traffic, this Azure service operates at Layer 7 and adds HTTP-aware features such as URL-path-based routing, SSL termination, and a Web Application Firewall.
clues.explain: Application Gateway is a Layer 7 load balancer and application delivery controller. Its awareness of HTTP allows it to route traffic to different backend pools based on URL paths or hostnames, and its integrated WAF can detect and block common web exploits.

clues.clue: This Azure Storage service is designed for unstructured data such as images, videos, and backup files — it is the most common storage type within an Azure Storage account.
clues.explain: Blob (Binary Large Object) storage is optimized for storing massive amounts of unstructured data. It supports three access tiers — Hot, Cool, and Archive — to balance cost against how frequently data is accessed.

clues.clue: This is the Azure Blob Storage access tier intended for data that is rarely accessed, costs the least per gigabyte stored, but requires several hours to retrieve and has a minimum storage duration of 180 days.
clues.response: What is the Archive access tier?
clues.explain: The Archive tier offers the lowest storage cost in Azure Blob Storage but is offline storage — data must be 'rehydrated' before it can be read, which can take up to 15 hours. It is suited for long-term retention such as compliance archives.

clues.clue: This Azure Storage redundancy option replicates data to the paired region in addition to making three copies in the primary region, providing protection against a full regional disaster.
clues.explain: GRS stores three synchronous copies in the primary region (like LRS) and then asynchronously replicates a copy to the Microsoft-defined paired region. This protects against a complete regional outage at the cost of higher per-gigabyte pricing.

clues.clue: This Azure Storage redundancy option is the CHEAPEST available, storing only three copies of data within a SINGLE datacenter in the primary region — it does not protect against a datacenter-level failure.
clues.explain: LRS writes three synchronous copies of each object within one physical datacenter. While it protects against disk or rack failures, a fire, flood, or power failure affecting the entire datacenter would cause data loss, making it unsuitable for critical workloads.

clues.clue: This Azure database service is a globally distributed NoSQL offering that guarantees single-digit-millisecond read and write latency, supports multiple data models, and offers five tunable consistency levels.
clues.explain: Cosmos DB is Microsoft's planet-scale NoSQL database. Its five consistency levels — from Strong down to Eventual — let developers balance read latency against data freshness. Data is transparently replicated across any Azure regions the customer selects.

clues.clue: This Microsoft cloud service — formerly known as Azure Active Directory — provides identity and access management for Azure, Microsoft 365, and third-party applications.
clues.explain: Microsoft Entra ID (rebranded from Azure AD in 2023) is Microsoft's cloud-based identity platform. It handles authentication via passwords, MFA, and passwordless methods, and authorization through role assignments and Conditional Access policies.

clues.clue: In Azure's resource hierarchy, this is the logical container that holds related resources such as virtual machines, storage accounts, and virtual networks — deleting it cascades and removes everything inside.
clues.explain: Every Azure resource must belong to exactly one resource group. Resource groups are used to organize resources by lifecycle, environment, or application — deleting the resource group is a single operation that simultaneously removes all contained resources.

clues.clue: Unlike the Contributor role -- which can fully manage resources but cannot grant access to others -- this is the most permissive built-in Azure RBAC role at a given scope, adding the ability to assign roles to other users.
clues.explain: The Owner Azure RBAC role has full access to manage all resources at its scope AND can assign Azure RBAC roles to others; Contributor can manage resources but cannot assign roles. (RBAC roles are separate from Microsoft Entra ID directory roles like Global Administrator.)

clues.clue: In the Azure resource hierarchy, this level sits ABOVE subscriptions and allows an organization to apply policies and RBAC assignments that cascade down to all subscriptions and resources within it.
clues.explain: Management groups are containers for subscriptions. An enterprise can organize subscriptions into a tree of management groups and assign Azure Policy or RBAC at the management group level; those assignments automatically inherit down through all child subscriptions and resources.

clues.clue: This Microsoft Entra ID feature evaluates signals such as user location, device compliance state, and sign-in risk to dynamically allow, block, or require multi-factor authentication before granting access to a resource.
clues.explain: Conditional Access is a Zero Trust control plane in Microsoft Entra ID. It applies if-then logic — for example, 'if a user signs in from an unmanaged device in an unknown location, then require MFA and block legacy authentication' — before issuing an access token.

clues.clue: This free Azure service analyzes your deployed resources and produces personalized recommendations across five pillars: Reliability, Security, Performance, Cost, and Operational Excellence.
clues.explain: Azure Advisor continuously monitors resource configuration and usage telemetry and surfaces actionable recommendations — such as right-sizing underutilized VMs or enabling soft-delete on storage accounts — without any additional cost to the customer.

clues.clue: Use this Azure tool BEFORE deploying any resources to estimate the expected monthly cost of a proposed Azure architecture based on chosen services, regions, and usage quantities.
clues.response: What is the Azure Pricing Calculator?
clues.explain: The Pricing Calculator (calculator.azure.com) allows architects to configure specific Azure services and receive a cost estimate before committing to a deployment. It is distinct from the TCO Calculator, which compares on-premises costs to Azure for migration planning.

clues.clue: This Azure governance feature allows administrators to prevent a resource from being deleted while still permitting configuration changes — it is one of two types of Azure resource locks.
clues.explain: Azure offers two resource lock types: CanNotDelete blocks deletion but allows reads and modifications, while ReadOnly blocks both modifications and deletion. Locks apply to all users regardless of RBAC role and must be explicitly removed before the protected action can be taken.

clues.clue: While Azure RBAC controls WHO can perform actions on resources, this Azure service controls WHAT types of resources can be created and enforces organizational standards — with effects such as Deny, Audit, and DeployIfNotExists.
clues.explain: Azure Policy evaluates resources against defined rules and can deny non-compliant resource creation, audit existing resources, or automatically remediate non-compliance. It is complementary to RBAC: RBAC manages permissions for users, while Policy governs allowed resource configurations.

clues.clue: This Azure service extends Azure management capabilities — including Azure Policy, RBAC, and Azure Monitor — to servers, Kubernetes clusters, and databases running on-premises or in other clouds.
clues.explain: Azure Arc projects non-Azure resources into the Azure Resource Manager control plane, giving them an Azure resource ID. This allows organizations to apply the same governance policies, role assignments, and monitoring configurations to on-premises and multi-cloud resources that they use for native Azure resources.
